4.text: Three methods of voluntary death are known to the Chukchee, — death

5.text: by stabbing with a knife or spear, death by strangulation, and death by

6.text: shooting. The last method is used much less frequently than the others.

7.text: The bow is never used, only the rifle. It seems, therefore, that this method

8.text: has come into use quite recently. The reason for using the rifle is that death

9.text: is more sudden and less painful. The people who kill the person desiring to

10.text: die are called “assistants” or “followers,” like those in the funeral ceremony.¹

11.text: When death is inflicted by stabbing, the mortal stroke must be given by men.

12.text: Women are not allowed to take part in the execution. The knife of the

13.text: person being killed has to be used. Then the death-stroke is less painful.

14.text: After death the wound has to be sewed up with thread. The knife is carried

15.text: to the funeral place and left there. A death stroke dealt by the hand of a

16.text: son is not painful, that given by the hand of a complete stranger is extremely

17.text: painful. Therefore, when in a strange camp, while on a journey or at a fair,

18.text: voluntary death is executed by other means than stabbing. When the person

19.text: is stabbed with a spear, his face is usually covered with a piece of skin or

20.text: with a shawl. Often he takes his position in the inner room, close to the

21.text: entrance. The executioner stands in the outer room, holding his spear for-

22.text: ward, and the man who desires to be killed takes the spear-head with both

23.text: his hands and points it against his heart. Then he gives a signal for the

24.text: death-stroke. Both in stabbing with the knife and with the spear, and also

25.text: in shooting with the rifle, the blow is given from the front, never from behind.

26.text: While only men are allowed to execute the wish of a person who desires to

27.text: die a bloody death, women may also assist in killing persons by strangling.

28.text: The wife of the man who is to die holds his head on her knees wrapped in

29.text: a shawl, while two men pull from both sides at a rope put around his neck.

30.text: If the man struggles too much, the woman “smoothes his hands” (i. e., keeps

31.text: them down with both her hands), or, if her strength is not sufficient, another

32.text: woman aids her. In one or two cases I listened to a description of strangling

33.text: from the lips of women who had held the heads of their dying husbands on

34.text: their knees. They spoke of it with much composure, and related how the

35.text: strangled man kicked with hands and feet, and how they kept him quiet.

36.text: After the desire to die is proclaimed aloud, the execution must be done

37.text: speedily, — if possible, on the same day or the next one, — for the keˊlet

38.text: hover about after the promise has been made, and if they have to wait too

39.text: long, they may lose patience and take some other person. Previous to his

40.text: last hours, the person is treated with fat meat and “alien food,” and all his
